newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds seen taking breather before moving higher.
newsitem.headline: Bunds seen taking breather before moving higher.

text.p: Bund futures were expected to continue taking a breather from recent strong gains on Friday ahead of U.S. inflation data, but traders remain confident that the market's direction remains higher.

The DTB Bund futures contract was down seven basis points in late trade on Thursday, having spent the day moving between 102.53 and 102.93 -- a range that could roughly limit Friday's trade until U.S. producer price data is released at 1230 GMT.
"The bond market is on a nice little trend and Bunds are having their share of the action," said Stuart Trow, analyst at Norinchukin International Plc in London.
The Bundesbank summer news conference had scant impact on prices with little surprising news emerging on the domestic economy or inflation.
Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer repeated his view there is more to monetary union than Maastricht deficit criteria and that German economic stagnation appears to have been overcome.
Although German inflation is little threat to the market, he added that consumer prices have been boosted of late by seasonal factors.
One of the major features of the market's recent climb has been a flattening of the yield curve.

Bear Stearns wrote in a market commentary that they expected the yield curve to continue its flattening trend with the spread between two- and 10-year maturities targeting 200 basis points -- a level it has not seen since February 28.

The investment house said over the next three to four months, it expected the curve to narrow to 175 basis points on the back of slow, low-inflation growth at the same time that increasing amounts of new supply are coming in to the short end of the yield curve.
The curve stood at 207 basis points on Thursday with short maturities underperforming.
"The flattening trade is the one that will pay off," Trow said.
The benchmark cash 10-year Bund, meanwhile, was down to 103.18 from 103.36 on Wednesday to yield 5.56 percent.
Traders said Friday's PPI numbers are the next major focus in the market, but that given the market's mood, Treasuries and Bunds could climb on anything but a much stronger-than-expected figure.
